parsed.explanation: No criminalisation, no trans-specific offence, targeting, detention or facility rule is documented, and a 2018 equality reform is a positive climate signal. However the only societal finding is dated 2015 stigma, gender-identity coverage of the reform is unresolved, and no trans-specific violence, police, border or remedy evidence is documented. In this thin-data dossier silence is not safety, so unknowns keep it below documented-protection jurisdictions, while absence of any known traveler-facing exposure keeps it above administrative universal-exposure cases.

entry_documents.protection: No document-mismatch offence or entry screening rule documented; no criminalisation of same-sex conduct.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor uses home passport; absence of domestic marker-change is a resident gap, not visitor exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.protection: No detention, prison-placement or verification practice documented.

federal_state_facilities.protection: No bathroom, ward or facility restriction documented; no subnational variation documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2015 report recorded societal stigma toward LGBT people, predating 2018 reform; no documented trans-specific law or enforcement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No criminalisation of consensual same-sex conduct; sexual-orientation discrimination unlawful since 2018.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: 2018 reform may signal tolerant institutions, but whether gender identity is enumerated is unresolved.

minors_guardians.interaction: No age-dependent entry, care or facility rule documented for minors or guardians.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence, police harassment or extortion documented; dated stigma only.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No police or violence data documented; 2018 equality reform is the only cited legal signal.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence in thin, dated record is not evidence of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No complaint mechanism, tribunal decision or enforcement under equality guarantee documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Constitutional equality guarantee on sexual orientation since 2018, practical operation unassessed.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved gender-identity scope prevents crediting a documented trans remedy.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.55-B has documented routine secondary screening, delay and discretionary refusal. This dossier documents no such universal exposure, so it sits higher, though unknowns prevent a larger gap.
0.65-A documents brief questioning plus working complaint, apology and compensation. This case has no documented remedy for gender identity, so it sits slightly below 0.65 despite no known exposure.

0.75-C documents accepted matching markers, trained border officers and appeal/compensation for detention. None of that traveler-facing protection is documented here, so this rates materially below 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is one national system: no criminalisation and a 2018 sexual-orientation equality reform, with no documented subnational difference, traveler-facing restriction, targeting, detention, facility or care rule. The operative risk is uncertainty itself—dated stigma, unresolved gender-identity coverage, and no documented recourse or violence data. That places it above known universal-exposure cases but below jurisdictions with documented, working trans protections.
